passages.note: Floor vote on HB2785, an omnibus elections bill; Kolodin voted Yea.
Bill status page shows Kolodin as prime sponsor of HB2785, signed into law as Chapter 1.

passages.provision_quote: Beginning in 2026, aT ANY VOTING LOCATION THE VOTER MAY CHOOSE TO PROVIDE IDENTIFICATION WHEN PRESENTING THE VOTER'S MAILED EARLY BALLOT, AND IF SO THE ELECTION OFFICIAL SHALL:
passages.note: HB2785 is a multi-subject elections bill; its only new identification clause is an optional ID-verification path for mail ballots, not a mandate on every mail ballot.

rows.reasoning: HB2785 (2024), which Kolodin sponsored and voted for, is an omnibus elections bill covering precincts, sample ballots, early ballot requests, signature verification, canvassing and recounts, with a new identification clause letting a voter 'choose to provide identification when presenting the voter's mailed early ballot' — an optional path, not a requirement on every mail ballot. No statement ties his vote or sponsorship to that specific clause, so no passage establishes any rung from 'Require no identification to vote' through 'Require documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote.'
